title: Deliver on time, get paid, and know your real hourly rate
course_title: Freelancing Fundamentals: Package, Price and Deliver Paid Work

say: Deliver on time, get paid, and know your real hourly rate.
This is the video for module three of Freelancing Fundamentals.
Clients come back to freelancers who are reliable, not only talented. Reliable means three things. You deliver what was agreed.

panel.heading: Reliable beats talented
items: Never make the client chase you

say: You deliver when you said.

panel.heading: Reliable beats talented
items: Never make the client chase you

say: And the client never has to chase you for news.

panel.heading: Reliable beats talented
items: Never make the client chase you

say: Then that good work must become money in your account, and you must check that it really pays.

panel.heading: Reliable beats talented
items: Never make the client chase you

say: Stage one, kick-off. Confirm the scope, collect every material the client promised, and say when the first draft will arrive.

panel.heading: The five-stage delivery workflow
items: Revisions, all changes in one message

say: Stage two, plan backwards. For example, Zainab needs 15 hours for 12 designs. She adds about 20 percent buffer, making 18 hours, and plans to finish on day 6 of 7.
When a power cut cost her 3 hours, she still delivered a day early.

panel.heading: The five-stage delivery workflow
items: Revisions, all changes in one message

say: Stage three, draft and self-check. Tick every item in the scope. Errors in names, prices and phone numbers are the ones clients notice first and forgive least.

panel.heading: The five-stage delivery workflow
items: Revisions, all changes in one message

say: Stage four, revisions. Ask the client to put all changes in one message per round. Scattered voice notes are the fastest way to miss a change.

panel.heading: The five-stage delivery workflow
items: Revisions, all changes in one message

say: Stage five, handover. Name files clearly, send the format the client needs, and check the share link opens.

panel.heading: The five-stage delivery workflow
items: Revisions, all changes in one message

say: If something will be late, say so as soon as you know, not on the deadline day. Clients forgive an early warning far more easily than a silent delay.

panel.heading: The five-stage delivery workflow
items: Revisions, all changes in one message
panel.rule: Bad news early, with a solution and a new date

say: An invoice is a formal request for payment. Send one for every job, even for friends, and number them in order so you can find them later.

card.title: Zainab's invoice
card.note: Balance due before final files are released.

say: Zainab lists each piece of work: 60,000 for the posts, 15,000 for the extra posts and 12,000 for the flyer. That is 87,000 naira.

card.title: Zainab's invoice
card.note: Balance due before final files are released.

say: Then she takes off the deposit she already received, 30,000 naira.

card.title: Zainab's invoice

say: The balance due is 57,000 naira. The client sees exactly how it was reached, so there is nothing to argue about.

say: Most late payments are disorganisation, not bad faith. Stay calm, keep each reminder short, and attach the invoice again. On the due date, send a friendly reminder.

panel.heading: When payment is late
items: 3 days late: ask if there is a problem
7 days late: work and files on hold

say: At 3 days late, ask if there is any problem with the invoice.

panel.heading: When payment is late
items: 3 days late: ask if there is a problem
7 days late: work and files on hold

say: At 7 days late, a firmer note. Further work and final files are on hold until payment, as agreed.

panel.heading: When payment is late
items: 3 days late: ask if there is a problem
7 days late: work and files on hold

say: After that, call. For large sums, ask a trusted adviser.

panel.heading: When payment is late

7 days late: work and files on hold

say: This is why the deposit matters. And if you met the client on a platform, keep payment on the platform, or you lose its protection.

panel.rule: Send previews for approval; final files after full payment

say: Being busy and being profitable are not the same. Your effective hourly rate is money received divided by all your working hours, paid and unpaid.

card.title: A busy month that paid too little
card.note: Effective rate = money received / all hours worked.

say: Amaka received 180,000 naira.

card.title: A busy month that paid too little
card.note: Effective rate = money received / all hours worked.

say: She spent 60 billable hours on those jobs, so 3,000 naira an hour.

card.title: A busy month that paid too little
card.note: Effective rate = money received / all hours worked.

say: But she also spent 30 hours on outreach, calls and admin. Over 90 hours, she earned only 2,000 naira an hour, less than half her minimum.
Her tracker showed why: unplanned revisions, and 12 hours on free samples. So she now limits revisions to 2 rounds and free samples to 30 minutes.

card.title: A busy month that paid too little
card.note: Effective rate = money received / all hours worked.

say: To remember. Plan backwards with a buffer. Check your work against the scope. Send an itemised invoice for every job.
Chase late payment calmly. And review your numbers each month, testing one change at a time.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Plan backwards, with about 20 percent buffer
Itemised, numbered invoice for every job
Chase late payment calmly, on a schedule
Review your numbers monthly, one change
